hypothesis: Untried rung: profile-guided optimization. The workload is branchy and dispatch-heavy (EVM opcode dispatch, MDBX B-tree comparisons, jsonrpsee routing), the kind of code where PGO's block layout and inlining decisions pay off. build-pgo.sh instruments, trains on the same light+heavy eth_call mix, merges the profiles and rebuilds with -Cprofile-use, keeping the family's target-cpu in both passes. Expect 3-10%.
llm_commentary: PGO is the first confirmed win since the four code changes: m9g 4.72s [4.76/4.75/4.65] → 4.43s [4.45/4.41/4.42], -6.1% against the same-boot control, with fully disjoint ranges and a tighter spread (0.04s vs 0.11s). Cost per run falls $0.000513 → $0.000482. This supersedes the previous champion (4.59s on the 10-28 boot) and is the best figure measured on any box except m8azn.3xlarge's 4.51s, which costs 3x more per run. It took three attempts to land, and the fixes are the finding: build with an explicit --target so cargo does not instrument (and then run) build scripts and proc macros, and link the instrumented pass with lld, because the instrumented binary overflows aarch64's +-128MB branch range and -Ccode-model=large is unusable there (it rejects ELF TLS, which foldhash needs). x86_64 is still blocked by a rustc LLVM 23.1 SIGILL while instrumenting the reth crate. The gain is consistent with a workload whose remaining hot paths are branchy dispatch (EVM opcodes, MDBX B-tree comparisons, jsonrpsee routing) rather than a single kernel; exp-pgo-maxperf tests whether fat LTO compounds with it.
